lead.headline: Bitcoin ETFs lose $1.8 billion in a week as rate-rise bets cool
lead.standfirst: Weekly figures confirmed heavy withdrawals from US spot bitcoin funds, but bitcoin edged higher overnight as traders scaled back bets on a big December Fed rise.
body: US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded about $1.79 billion of net outflows last week, The Block reported, citing SoSoValue data. It was the largest weekly outflow since late June and the fourth week in a row of withdrawals, led by about $1.37 billion from BlackRock's IBIT.

About $4.14 billion has left the funds so far in November, according to the report, and their total net assets stood at $71.35 billion on Friday, down from about $110 billion in mid-September. Analysts quoted by The Block linked the selling to risk reduction ahead of expected Fed rate rises, with one calling the outflows more structural.

Rate expectations eased slightly. CoinDesk reported that fed funds futures no longer price any chance of a half-point December rise, after the Nasdaq fell 10.4% last week, its worst week since March 2020. A quarter-point rise is still expected, and Cointelegraph cited CME FedWatch odds of about 91%.
Bitcoin traded near $61,470 on Kraken at 06:30 UK time on Monday, Kraken data showed, about 1% above Sunday evening and well clear of last week's two-year low near $55,000. Zcash traded near $786.
US markets and spot bitcoin ETFs reopen at 14:30 UK, giving the first test of fund demand this week.

headline: Bitcoin edged up to near $61,470 overnight while ZEC slipped to about $786. Weekly data showed $1.8 billion leaving US spot bitcoin ETFs, but bets on a half-point December Fed rise have gone.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition, Monday the twenty third of November. Bitcoin is near sixty one thousand five hundred dollars, up about one percent overnight. Zcash is near seven hundred and eighty six dollars, a little lower. New figures show about one point eight billion dollars left US spot bitcoin funds last week, the biggest weekly outflow since June. Traders have dropped bets on a half point Fed rate rise in December, though a quarter point rise is still expected. US markets and bitcoin funds open at half past two this afternoon. The next big event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.79 billion last week
stories.why: The Block, citing SoSoValue, put last week's net outflow at about $1.79 billion, the largest since June and a fourth straight losing week; IBIT accounted for about $1.37 billion. This updates the roughly $1.1 billion figure in earlier editions with the full week, and November's total outflow is about $4.14 billion.
stories.caveat: The Block's article gives last week's bitcoin low as both about $55,100 and about $55,700.

note.read: Fund holders kept cutting risk all week, so the weekend rebound happened without ETF support.
note.alt: Outflows often peak around sharp sell-offs; a slower pace this week would suggest the worst of the selling has passed.
note.change: Daily net inflows on two or more days this week would weaken the view that the outflows are structural.

stories.title: Half-point December Fed rise priced out after Nasdaq rout
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that futures no longer price a 50 basis point December rise, from about 10% ten days ago, after the Nasdaq's 10.4% weekly fall. A 25 basis point rise is still expected, with about a 60% chance of another in January; Cointelegraph cited about 91% FedWatch odds for December.

note.read: The market now sees the stock sell-off limiting how far the Fed goes, a small easing for risk assets including bitcoin.
note.alt: Fed officials such as Governor Cook still say policy is too loose, so hawkish speeches could bring the bigger-rise bets back.
note.change: Firm October core PCE inflation data or hawkish Fed speeches this week would revive the case for larger rises.

stories.title: Bitcoin edges up overnight to near $61,470
stories.why: Kraken showed Bitcoin near $61,470 at 06:30 UK, up about 1% from $60,840 at the evening edition, with a range of about $60,270 to $61,890 since midnight UK. The new evidence is that the weekend rebound held through the Asia session as US futures reopened.

note.read: Steady overnight buying suggests the rebound has survived its first test since futures reopened.
note.alt: Overnight trade is thin; the US open and ETF flows are the bigger test.
note.change: A fall back below $60,000 after the 14:30 UK open would undo the overnight gain.

stories.title: Bitcoin briefly sold for about $17,000 on Kraken's Canadian dollar market
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that BTC traded as low as C$24,250 (about US$17,000) on Kraken's CAD book early Saturday, about 70% below global prices. Kraken said it found no breach and that executed trades stand. A reminder that thin local-currency order books can print extreme prices; the main USD market was not affected and prices are back in line.

stories.title: ZEC slips to about $786
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $786 at 06:30 UK, against about $791 last night, after a range of roughly $775 to $803 since midnight UK. No market-moving ZEC news overnight.

stories.title: Zaino indexer release candidate moves to a new team
stories.why: Zaino 0.11.0-rc1, light-wallet indexing software for Zebra nodes, is the first release from Umbriel Systems rather than ZingoLabs, according to the Zcash forum post. It supports NU7 and Zebra 7; the post says earlier work stalled over a ZingoLabs disagreement, and ZingoLabs has released its own indexer. Background for the move away from zcashd.

stories.title: Fusionist's ACE bridge drained in third weekend exploit
stories.why: The Block reported that an attacker minted unbacked ACE tokens on Fusionist's bridge and sold them for about $2 million, after which traders redeemed about $3.7 million more. It follows the Chainflip and Cyber incidents this weekend; small for the wider market.

explained.title: Why one exchange can show a crazy price
body: An exchange runs a separate order book for each currency pair. A big market like bitcoin against US dollars has many buyers and sellers, but a smaller one like bitcoin against Canadian dollars may rely on a few market makers. If they pull out, a large sell order can fall through empty price levels and trade far below the global price, as CoinDesk reported happened on Kraken's Canadian dollar book on Saturday.
Such prints say little about the wider market, but they can trigger stop orders on that book. Prices in the main US dollar market are the better guide to where bitcoin really traded.
